comment: Chunk 2: I mapped each model species to the most likely human gene symbol(s) based on the display labels used in the model (e.g., YAP→YAP1, TAZ→WWTR1, SMAD2_3_4→SMAD2/SMAD3/SMAD4 components). Known complexes were expanded into their constituent gene products (e.g., Lats1_2→LATS1;LATS2; IKKa_b→CHUK;IKBKB; bcatenin_Hif1a_complex→CTNNB1;HIF1A; b_catenin_TCF4→CTNNB1;TCF7L2; ILK_Rictor→ILK;RICTOR; SMAD2_3_4→SMAD2/3/4). MicroRNA nodes were mapped to MIR gene names (miR-200_b/c, miR-29c, miR-34 family). Ambiguous phenotype/process nodes (Stress_Fibers, ApicalBasal_Pol, Horizontal_Pol, Migration, Fast_Migration, Self_Loop) were assigned representative, commonly implicated genes in those processes (e.g., stress fibers → actins/myosins ACTA2/ACTB/MYH9; apical–basal polarity → PARD3/PARD6B/PRKCI; planar/horizontal polarity → VANGL2/PRICKLE1/CELSR1; migration/invasion → MMP family). Standard synonyms and common aliases (e.g., ALK5 for TGFBR1, DPC4 for SMAD4, NF2/MERLIN, CTNNB1/beta-catenin) were included where relevant.

comment: Chunk 3: I mapped each model species to the most likely human gene(s) or canonical gene representatives used in cell-cycle, apoptosis and hypoxia signaling literature. Standard cyclins/CDKs and checkpoint kinases are mapped to their canonical gene symbols (e.g., CCND1→Cyclin D1, CCNA2→Cyclin A2, CCNB1→Cyclin B1, CDK1→CDK1, CHEK1→CHK1, PLK1→PLK1). Cell-cycle regulators and inhibitors use CDKN gene symbols (CDKN1A=p21, CDKN1B=p27, CDKN2B=p15). Rb and E2F/Myc/YAP maps are RB1, E2F1, MYC, YAP1. Apoptosis components use TNFSF10 (TRAIL), TNFRSF10A/B (DR4/DR5), CASP8, CASP3/2. Hypoxia sensors/hydroxylases mapped to EGLN1/2 (PHD2/PHD1) and HIF1AN (FIH); HIF states to HIF1A. ROS was mapped to NADPH oxidase family members (NOX4 primary). Replication/replication-licensing nodes mapped to ORC/CDC6/CDT1 and MCM/PCNA representatives; Pre_RC listed as key components (ORC1, CDC6, CDT1). APC/C (pAPC) represented by core ANAPC subunits (ANAPC1/4/11) and APC regulators by CDC20 and FZR1 (Cdh1). Kinetochores represented by core kinetochore genes (NDC80, KNL1, MIS12, ZWINT) as proxies for unattached/attached kinetochore states. MicroRNAs are mapped to their host/primary identifiers (MIR17HG, MIR17, MIR200B/C). Where model nodes represent activity states (e.g., Plk1_H, pVHL, pAPC, Hif1a_High/ basal) I used the primary encoding gene plus common protein/state names. Where a complex or multi-subunit entity is implied (Pre-RC, ORC, APC/C, DR4_5, PHD1_2), I listed representative constituent genes as separate typed groups.

comment: Chunk 1: Provided mappings favor canonical human gene symbols commonly used in signaling/EMT literature and the model context. For mechanotransduction/density nodes I mapped CellDensity_High to NF2/MERLIN (density sensor) and CDH1 (adhesion marker); CellDensity_Low to YAP1/WWTR1 (density-sensitive Hippo effectors). ECM/Stiff_ECM mapped to abundant matrix genes (FN1, COL1A1) used to represent substrate and stiffness. GF/GF_High were mapped to prototypical growth factors (EGF/HBEGF/FGF2) because the model uses RTK signaling; RTK was mapped to EGFR/ERBB2/PDGFRB as common receptor tyrosine kinases. Adaptor and Ras‑MAPK nodes map to their canonical genes: SHC1, GRB2, SOS1, RAS family (KRAS/HRAS/NRAS), RAF (RAF1/BRAF), MEK (MAP2K1/2), ERK (MAPK1/3). PI3K/PIP3/p110 nodes map to catalytic PI3K subunits (PIK3CA as top choice, then PIK3CB/PIK3CD); PDK1→PDPK1; AKT pools→AKT1 (AKT/PKB). mTOR complexes were expanded into known core components: mTOR, RICTOR, MAPKAP1 (SIN1), MLST8 for mTORC2; MTOR, RPTOR, MLST8 for mTORC1. Regulators and effectors mapped to their genes: TSC2, RHEB, PRAS40→AKT1S1, 4EBP1→EIF4EBP1, eIF4E→EIF4E, S6K→RPS6KB1. FOXO1/3 and GSK3→FOXO1/FOXO3/GSK3B. PLCγ/IP3/DAG/Ca2+ nodes were mapped to the canonical enzymes or receptors they represent (PLCG1 for PLCγ; ITPR1 for IP3 receptor; PRKCA as a DAG-responsive kinase; CALM1 as a Ca2+ sensor). Ubiquitin ligase Nedd4L mapped to NEDD4L. Adhesion molecules mapped to common family genes: Integrin→ITGB1/ITGA5, ILK→ILK, FAK→PTK2, focal adhesions→PXN (paxillin) as a marker. Nectin/Necl family mapped to PVRL3 (NECTIN3) and PVR (CD155/Necl5). SPRY2 mapped to SPRY2. Junctional cadherin/catenin complexes mapped to CDH1 (E‑cadherin), CTNNB1 (β‑catenin), CTNNA1 (α‑catenin). p21 mRNA mapped to CDKN1A (p21). Where species were explicitly labeled as high/active (e.g., Src_H, PI3K_H, p110_H) I gave the same gene with the implication of an activated/hyperactive state. Where multiple isoforms are possible I listed the most common/oncogenic isoform first (e.g., PIK3CA, KRAS, MAPK1, AKT1).
